where we use the notation of \cref{NC_disc_met} for $x_{i},y_{i},A_{i},B_{i}$, and $W$ is an RKHS of vector fields induced by spatial kernel $K_{p}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated decomposition gives <N(C),N(S)> = \sum_{i,j} k_p(x_i,y_j)<A_i,B_j>, but the paper's own Theorem thm:added-2 (quoted from NCThesis) states the inner product is (pi^2/4) \sum k_p<A_i,B_j> with the same A_i,B_i. Each delta weight is therefore short by a factor pi/2 (the product by pi^2/4). Independent check: the normal cone at a curve vertex is a spherical lune, and \int_{u.f1<=0, u.f2<=0} u dH^2(u) = -(pi/2)(f1+f2) (for a right-angle corner the integral is (-pi/2,-pi/2,0)), so the correct weight is (pi/2)A_i, confirming the theorem and refuting the decomposition as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the decomposition by N(C) = (pi/2) \sum_i \delta_{x_i} A_i and N(S) = (pi/2) \sum_j \delta_{y_j} B_j, the unique rescaling consistent with Theorem thm:added-2 as quoted in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: The curve normal-cycle representation used as compression input is mis-scaled: inner products and distances computed from it are 4/pi^2 (resp. 2/pi) times the values of the normal-cycle metric of Theorem thm:added-2, so the decomposition does not represent the normal cycle it claims to, and any curve compression or registration built on it inherits the wrong quantitative scale (a global rescaling, so registration minimizers are unaffected but all reported metric values are wrong).
issues.title: Dirac decomposition of discrete curve normal cycles is missing a factor of pi/2 and contradicts the paper's own curve metric theorem
issues.why_classification: A single forced factor (pi/2 per weight) restores consistency with the quoted theorem; the repair is short, local and routine, needs no new lemma or construction, and preserves every substantive claim and guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: For a semicircle C of the unit circle with bisector direction beta_T, \int_C u dH^1(u) = 2 beta_T (equivalently, the centroid of a semicircular wire is at distance 2/pi from the centre, and the arc length pi gives pi . (2/pi) = 2). The claimed value (pi/2) beta_T is false. The cylindrical edge weight per incident triangle is therefore 2 (f_hat,0) ^ (0, f x beta_T), not (pi/2) (f_hat,0) ^ (0, f_hat x beta_T); the derived coefficient -(pi/2) gamma_j should be -2 gamma_j, and the edge-term inner product becomes 4 \sum k_p<f_i,g_j><\sum n,\sum n'> instead of the pi^2/4 factor appearing in the quoted formula NC_disc_met. The false value is exactly what makes the paper's derivation formally reproduce the quoted theorem, so the error cannot be corrected locally without contradicting the quoted result.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must correct the integral to 2 beta_T, propagate the corrected factor 2 through the cylindrical weights, and reconcile the resulting edge-term constant (4 in the inner product) with the pi^2/4 factor quoted from NCpaper, which the source as written cannot do.
issues.overall_effect: The cylindrical component coefficients, the Dirac delta form NC_delta, the real-valued embedding realembedding, and hence the compressed normal-cycle target used in all downstream compression experiments and LDDMM applications are unreliable; the advertised agreement with the cited normal-cycle metric (thm:added-1) fails for the edge term.
issues.title: Half-circle unit-normal integral is miscalculated: the source claims (pi/2) beta_T but the integral over a semicircle of the unit circle is 2 beta_T
issues.why_classification: The root is a false computation on which the central decomposition rests; the only repair (use 2 beta_T) changes the edge coefficient to -2 gamma_j and thereby destroys the claimed agreement with the quoted metric formula NC_disc_met, and the source contains no consistent alternative derivation. Every supported resolution either abandons the advertised consistency with the cited normal-cycle metric or requires re-deriving the constants against the cited literature: a major loss for the paper's central construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the quantity $A_{i} := \sum_{k}{f_{k}^{i}/\lvert f_{k}^{i}\rvert}$ is defined as the sum of normalized edges attached to the boundary vertex $x_{i}$, oriented outwards from $x_{i}$

issues.failure_explanation: Substituting the (correct) hemisphere integral pi . alpha into the assembly boundarysph (full sphere plus one hemisphere S_{f/|f|}^+ per incident edge) gives boundary weight pi A_k per vertex, so the boundary-term inner product produced by the paper's derivation (and retained in NC_delta) is pi^2 \sum k_p<A_i,B_j>. The paper's own Theorem thm:added-1 states the boundary term is (pi^2/4) \sum k_p<A_i,B_j>, which requires weight (pi/2) A_k. Direct computation confirms the smaller value: the normal cone at a boundary vertex is a spherical lune and \int_{u.f1<=0, u.f2<=0} u dH^2(u) = -(pi/2)(f1+f2) (for a right-angle corner: (-pi/2,-pi/2,0)); e.g. for a single triangle corner the sphere-plus-hemispheres assembly gives pi(f1+f2) while the actual normal-cycle weight is (pi/2)(f1+f2). So the boundary assembly overcounts by a factor of 2, independently of the half-circle integral error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the boundary-vertex contribution from the spherical lunes of the incident triangle corners (including the endpoint-sphere cancellations), which yields weight (pi/2) A_k, and replace the coefficient pi by pi/2 in the spherical component conclusion, in NC_delta, and in realembedding; this restores agreement with the quoted boundary term of thm:added-1.
issues.overall_effect: The boundary-term weights in NC_delta (and the inconsistent pi/2 boundary coefficient in realembedding) are wrong, so the decomposition does not reproduce the quoted surface metric NC_disc_met for shapes with boundary; normal-cycle inner products computed from the decomposition for bounded surfaces are off by a factor 4 in the boundary term, and the paper's claimed consistency check is false.
issues.title: Spherical component boundary weight is twice the value required by the paper's quoted surface metric theorem
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained recomputation (spherical-lune integrals) that changes only the boundary coefficient from pi to pi/2; it leaves the quoted theorem, the decomposition architecture, and all advertised rates and guarantees intact, so a recognizably comparable result survives without new global proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Multiplying out NC_delta using <\delta_x tau, \delta_y tau'>_{W*} = k_p(x,y)<tau,tau'> gives edge-term product pi^2 \sum k_p(c_j,c_j')<f_j,f_j'><\sum_{T ni e_j} n_{T,f_j}, \sum_{T' ni e_j'} n_{T',f_j'}> and boundary product pi^2 \sum k_p<A_i,A_i'>, whereas the quoted formula NC_disc_met has pi^2/4 in both terms: the decomposition is a factor 4 too large, so the claimed agreement check is false. Independently, the edge coefficient pi in NC_delta is twice the coefficient -pi/2 derived in the cylindrical component subsection (with gamma redefined by a sign flip between the two displays), so the final formula does not follow even from the paper's own derivation. Matching the quoted theorem would require coefficient pi/2, which is incompatible both with the derivation as written (based on the false half-circle integral) and, after correcting that integral to 2 beta_T, with the true value 2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must choose edge and boundary coefficients that are simultaneously consistent with the (corrected) cylindrical computation and with the quoted metric NC_disc_met: the source supports no such choice, since the derivation yields -pi/2 (with the false integral) or -2 (with the correct integral 2 beta_T) while the quoted theorem requires pi/2.
issues.overall_effect: The central decomposition formula of the paper is unreliable: it is not the Dirac form of the normal cycle of the quoted metric, the consistency check it claims is false, and the edge and boundary terms are mis-normalized by different factors, so distances computed from the decomposition are not the normal-cycle distances of thm:added-1; the compression target for surfaces and all downstream experiments and applications inherit this.
issues.title: Dirac delta form NC_delta has coefficients inconsistent with the paper's own derivation and does not reproduce the quoted normal-cycle metric
issues.why_classification: The primary claim is the paper's central construction; no comparable version of NC_delta survives within the source, because every candidate coefficient is inconsistent with either the paper's own derivation or the quoted metric theorem, and the source provides no correct derivation to fall back on. Repairing requires essentially re-deriving the normal-cycle decomposition constants against the cited literature, a major loss.
